docRequirement: features-overview.md:227 (the footnote under the skills row) binds us to a settings-side equivalent of the frontmatter control it has just described: "Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in a skill's frontmatter to hide it from Claude entirely until you invoke it manually. This reduces context cost to zero for skills you only trigger yourself. For a skill you didn't write, set [`skillOverrides`](/docs/en/skills#override-skill-visibility-from-settings) in settings to do the same without editing its file." So the binding on THIS page is narrower than the full ladder: a settings key spelled exactly `skillOverrides` must be able to hide a skill from the model while leaving it manually invocable, for a skill whose SKILL.md the user does not own or want to edit, and it must cost zero context when set. The linked section (skills.md:635-663) supplies the shape the key must take: a map of skill name to one of `"on"` / `"name-only"` / `"user-invocable-only"` / `"off"`, absent means `"on"` (:652), written to `.claude/settings.local.json` (:637), with plugin skills explicitly exempt (:663). The state that discharges this page's sentence is `"user-invocable-only"` (skills.md:641-646: Listed to Claude = Hidden, in `/` menu = Yes).

Three concrete deltas: (1) no key of any spelling reaches skill visibility, so the four states, the absent-means-`"on"` default and the `.claude/settings.local.json` destination have no implementation; (2) `RuntimeSkillHandle` (views.ts:69-109) carries only the two frontmatter booleans, so the three consumers (prompt-builder.ts:405, custom-commands.ts:443, base-agent.ts:2141) have no override input to read even if one were parsed; (3) `skillOverrides` cannot even be PUT in our config.json today — `StoredConfigTopLevelSchema` is `.strict()` (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:208) over `StoredConfigKnownFields` (:143-202) and `loadStoredConfig` throws `UnsupportedStorageLayoutError` on any unknown top-level key (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:856-861), so a user who copies the documented snippet bricks config load rather than hiding a skill. userImpact: Concrete and reachable today, with the twist that the documented remedy actively breaks the app. Clone a repo that ships skills at `.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` (packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:37) or `.nessy-agent/skills/`, open it as a project, and there is no way to hide any of them from the model without committing a frontmatter change into someone else's repository, deleting the directory, or refusing project trust wholesale. In the Skills list the row offers Show in Finder, Send to workspace, and a Delete greyed out and labelled "managed by project" (SkillsListPanel.tsx:68, :95-96); SkillInfoPage has no visibility control either. Every such skill keeps its full name-plus-description line in `<available_skills>` on every request of every session inside Pi's cached prefix (prompt-builder.ts:97-105, :403-447) — the exact context cost the doc sentence says this key removes — and because that listing is capped at `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (:105), unwanted entries can push wanted ones past the budget until the model is told "(N more skills not listed — ask the user which to use.)" (:441-444). And a user who follows the page and writes `"skillOverrides": { "deploy": "off" }` into our config.json gets a hard `UnsupportedStorageLayoutError` on load (storage.ts:856-861) rather than a hidden skill — a silent no-op would be the gentler failure.
